deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. X is a topological space and I is an ordered set. We are given an increasing map i ↦ X_i into the closed subsets of X; condition (1'b) is i ≤ j ⇒ X_i ⊆ X_j.

The earlier pages build a topological category with object space X_{Δ0} = ∐_i X_i and morphism space X_{Δ1} = {(x,i,j) : x ∈ X_i, i ≤ j}. Its nerve has components X_{Δr} = {(x,i_0,…,i_r) : x ∈ X_{i_0}, i_0 ≤ … ≤ i_r} = ∐_{i_* ∈ N(I)_r} X_{i_0}. These are the r-fold fibre products of X_{Δ1} over X_{Δ0}.

This page makes the structure maps explicit. For an increasing α: Δ_{r'} → Δ_r, the map α^*: X_{Δr} → X_{Δr'} is (x,i_*) ↦ (x, i_*∘α). This is well defined because i_{α(0)} ≥ i_0, so x ∈ X_{i_0} ⊆ X_{i_{α(0)}}. In other words, X_{Δ*} is the sub-simplicial space of the product of the constant simplicial space X with the nerve I_{Δ*} = N(I).

In modern terms, X_{Δ*} is the Bousfield–Kan simplicial replacement (Grothendieck construction / nerve of the category of elements) of the diagram I → Top, i ↦ X_i. Its geometric realisation is hocolim_I X_i, augmented to X.

Remark a): everything generalises if I is replaced by a small category C and i ↦ X_i by a functor from C to the category of closed subsets of X and inclusions.

Remark b): starting from a bare family (X_i), one could order I by i ≤ j ⇔ X_i ⊆ X_j. But the chosen presentation does not need i ↦ X_i to be injective, still less an order-embedding (X_i ⊆ X_j ⇒ i ≤ j, the converse of (1'b)).

Purpose: this is the combinatorial scaffolding for describing a stratified space or topos (strata or closures indexed by a poset) by a simplicial space over X. The next page will exploit its étale and local properties to get descent or simplicial-topos descriptions of the stratified topos.
errors: Terminology: 'semi-simplicial' (½ simplicial) is used in the old Eilenberg–Zilber sense. Since all increasing α, degeneracies included, act on X_{Δ*}, it is in fact a simplicial space in modern terms.

Not on this page but relevant to it: the next page claims the maps α^* with α(0) ≠ 0, and X_{Δr} → X, are local homeomorphisms. With X_i closed and X_{Δr} = ∐ X_{i_0} carrying the coproduct topology, these maps are disjoint unions of closed embeddings (X_{i_0} ↪ X_{i_α(0)}, X_{i_0} ↪ X). Those are not local homeomorphisms in general. The claim needs a different topology or an open-set setting.
The equation label (15) is reused on the next page (duplicate numbering).

ideas.what: Simplicial space X_{Δ*} = ∐_{i_0≤…≤i_r} X_{i_0}, the nerve of the topological category of the poset-indexed family of closed subsets, embedded in X × N(I)
ideas.modern_name: Bousfield–Kan simplicial replacement / Grothendieck construction; homotopy colimit of a poset-indexed closed cover (Segal's Mayer–Vietoris simplicial space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal 1968; Bousfield–Kan 1972; Thomason 1979 (hocolim via the Grothendieck construction)
ideas.where_published: Related nerve-of-cover and fibred-category constructions appear in SGA 4 (Vbis, hypercovers, by Saint-Donat/Deligne) and in Pursuing Stacks; this exact construction is unsure

ideas.what: Generalisation from a poset I to a small category C with a functor to closed subsets and inclusions
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy colimit over a category / category of elements
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA 1 VI / SGA 4 (fibred categories, Grothendieck construction)

ideas.what: Remark that the indexing map need not be injective nor an order-embedding (no converse of (1'b) required)
ideas.modern_name: Stratifications indexed by arbitrary posets via a monotone map (cf. Lurie's Higher Algebra, Appendix A; 'P-stratified spaces')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (HA Appendix A), Haine, Barwick–Glasman–Haine (Exodromy) for the poset-indexed formalism

missed.claim: In an unpublished 1981+ stratified-topos manuscript, Grothendieck uses poset-indexed closed families with an arbitrary monotone map to closed subsets (not required injective or an embedding). He builds a simplicial space over X × N(I), intending it as a model of the stratified topos. This anticipates in spirit the modern 'stratification as a continuous map to a poset' formalism and the simplicial or exodromic models of stratified homotopy types. The mathematics on this page itself is routine.
missed.quote: il n'est pas nécessaire de supposer que l'appl. croissante I → ens. des parties fermées de X soit injective, et encore moins que ce soit un plongement d'ens. ordonnés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck's own route to poset-stratified topoi, relevant to the history of exit-path and exodromy results (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie, Barwick–Glasman–Haine). It is not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard simplicial-replacement / nerve construction plus terminological remarks. Its only interest is historical, as part of Grothendieck's unpublished stratified-topos program with a modern-looking poset formalism.

'des parties fermées de X et des inclusions' reads more like 'des parties fermées de X et de leurs inclusions'.
